\subsection{Native Sim--Recon--Sim: A Target-Only DEV Test}

\input{tables/native_dev_results}

We attempt target reconstruction in each of 8 frozen RoboCasa365~\cite{robocasa365} instances across 2 layouts, using posed ideal RGB-D observations. The robot, controller, cameras, policy checkpoint, reset bank, instructions and native horizons remain fixed. The room and destination retain privileged native geometry; the reconstructed target uses a uniform material. This isolates a complete target-asset intervention, not room reconstruction or Gaussian rendering.

Table~\ref{tab:native-dev} retains every planned reset; 200/200 units have terminal records in this immutable snapshot. Build failure and abstention contribute zero service success while keeping native success unmeasured. Pending episodes do not become failures. Native predicates retain their original contact/body-origin semantics; they do not certify whole-mesh containment or independently corresponding object frames.

B0 uses TRELLIS; B3 selects from TRELLIS/ReconViaGen proposals with a bounded registration retry. B4 uses measured contact, support, public-surface fit and destination-access evidence to choose bounded actions; BM uses the same action bank in fixed order. Passing these construction checks is not independent physics validation. These DEV observations do not establish TEST preservation, sim--real transfer, or a room-scale manipulation benefit.

B4 raises conditional success but lowers success over all planned episodes relative to B3: stricter acceptance exposes a coverage penalty rather than an unconditional manipulation gain.
